properties.Name: Marines, NC
properties.Description: A civilian riverfront farming and fishing village completely erased and demolished when the War Department condemned the lower basin.

properties.Name: Montford Point
properties.Description: The segregated base facility established where African American recruits were trained following Executive Order 8802.

properties.Name: Courthouse Bay
properties.Description: Former historic settlement and county seat site repurposed for amphibious landing craft training and naval support.

properties.Name: Hadnot Point
properties.Description: Former agricultural land transformed into the administrative core and central industrial barracks complex of the base. This is the MAIN place.

properties.Name: Browns Island
properties.Description: Coastal barrier island seized from civilian use and converted into an active naval and aerial live-fire bombardment range.

properties.Name: Stone Bay Rifle Range
properties.Description: Coastal farming property transformed into long-range small-arms marksmanship and specialized sniper ranges.

properties.Name: French Creek
properties.Description: Maritime creek basin cleared of local homesteads to build field training, logistics, and divisional camp facilities.

properties.Name: Peterfield Point
properties.Description: Riverfront point converted into airfield runways and hangars, later becoming Marine Corps Air Station New River.

properties.Name: Midway Park
properties.Description: Rapidly constructed federal defense housing development built inside the border to house civilian workers and military families.

properties.Name: Onslow Beach
properties.Description: Barrier beachfront taken by eminent domain for rehearsal of massive Pacific-bound amphibious assaults and ship-to-shore landings.

properties.Name: Jacksonville
properties.Description: County seat of around 800 residents suddenly turned into a boomtown border hub handling incoming labor and evicted families.

properties.Name: Kellumtown
properties.Description: Historic Black settlement near Hubert that served as an essential relocation haven for displaced Black families.

properties.Name: Verona
properties.Description: Western railway community where evicted white landowners resettled and built new agricultural holdings.

properties.Name: Sneads Ferry
properties.Description: Historic fishing community at the southern inlet that absorbed displaced fishermen and tied into coastal seafood routes.

properties.Name: MCAS Cherry Point
properties.Description: Constructed concurrently in Craven County as part of North Carolina's massive coastal WWII defense corridor.

properties.Name: Port of Morehead City
properties.Description: Deepwater shipping terminal that moved heavy naval armaments and marine logistical supplies bound for the base.

properties.Name: New Bern
properties.Description: Regional commercial and railroad hub routing inbound industrial materials and civilian construction crews south to the base.

properties.Name: Quantico, Virginia
properties.Description: Headquarters and command development center that directed the acquisition and construction of the New River barracks.

properties.Name: Parris Island
properties.Description: Primary Marine recruit depot linked to Camp Lejeune as part of the East Coast wartime infantry training pipeline.

properties.Name: Washington, D.C.
properties.Description: Seat of federal power where the War Department authorized condemnation letters and distributed $25 checks to landowners.
